description: Unstructured, tangential internal-tools maintainer. Run-on sentences, lowercase, asides, weak sentence boundaries. Stress-tests the heuristic extractor's precision-over-recall stance against messy real-world phrasing.

messages.text: so anyway we ended up going with sqlite for the little internal tool, way simpler than standing up postgres for something three people use
oh also — decision: we're calling it 'the widget' internally even though the doc says 'internal-tools-dashboard', don't let that confuse you
we tried just cron + a bash script for the nightly sync but it didn't work, kept silently failing and nobody noticed for a week
requirement: whatever we build next has to send a slack ping if it fails, learned that one the hard way lol
actually wait, the sync runs at 3am, not midnight, I keep saying midnight but that's wrong
the correct value for the retry count is 5 attempts, not 3, someone changed it last sprint
never touch the export script on Fridays, don't ask why
check the readme at ./scripts/sync/README.md if you're touching that job
here's the thing, https://internal.acme.example/wiki/sync-job has the full runbook, way more than I can type here, some people call it 'the sync wiki page' too
I always forget to update the doc after I change the cron schedule, so don't trust the doc, trust the crontab
constraint: the onboarding checklist lives in google docs — nobody moves it to the wiki till q3.

goldFacts.note: message 1 — heuristic 'going with X' decision pattern fires on the trailing clause

ALIAS CASE 1 (MISS BY DESIGN) — message 2 explicitly declares 'the widget' as a nickname for this project, but the heuristic extractor has no concept of entity aliasing; it does not match 'decision: we're calling it X' as a decision pattern at all (the DECISION_PATTERNS require 'use'/'chose'/'going with'/'decided'/'agreed'/'concluded' shapes, not 'calling it'). A probe using only 'the widget' will not resolve to this project. This is the sharpest alias case in the corpus — the entity itself, not just one fact, is aliased.

CORRECTION CASE (MISS BY DESIGN) — message 5's 'actually wait, X, not Y' phrasing has no 'is'/'should be' clause, so CORRECTION_PATTERNS does not match. Nothing is extracted. This is the same 'actually...not...' phrasing gap seen in the data-ml persona's AUC correction, confirming it's a systemic pattern-coverage gap rather than one-off phrasing.
message 6 — DOES match ('the correct value for X is Y' pattern)

goldFacts.value: never touch the export script on Fridays
goldFacts.note: CONSTRAINT CASE (MISS BY DESIGN) — message 7's 'never touch X on Y' does not match any CONSTRAINT_PATTERNS (those require can't/cannot/must not/should not/won't/requirement:/constraint:/have to/must/not allowed to) nor FAILED_PATTERNS (require 'didn't work'/'failed' framing). Nothing is extracted. Documents a real constraint-phrasing gap distinct from the 'never use X' PREFERENCE_PATTERNS match seen elsewhere (that pattern only fires for 'never use'/'never do', not 'never touch').
message 8 — deterministic relative-path artifact extraction (leading ./ matches RELATIVE_PATH_PATTERN)
ALIAS CASE 2 — message 9 also refers to the same URL as 'the sync wiki page'. No entity resolution exists; a probe on the alias alone will not find the fact. INTENTIONALLY scores 0 today.

goldFacts.note: AX-9 em-dash gold (added red-first): sentence-initial lowercase 'constraint:' label with an em-dash clause. Pre-fix the bare pattern's capture can't reach a [.,;] terminator within 80 chars (the dash isn't one), so NOTHING extracts. Flips when the anchored label pattern + dash terminators land.
